label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L=8-9) that start with j/t/u/k/v
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step feature: 98.8% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0, about to output the first original token), plus small weak activations on the last original token of L=9 sequences. It fires only for long sequences: L=9 (79% of mass) and L=8 (21%), never for L<=6 and barely for L=7. Within that, magnitude depends strongly on the first original token (the token about to be output): j is by far the strongest (36% of mass; top examples are all j-initial, reaching max 4.67), then t, u, k, v, s, p, i, b. Weak activations occur for other first tokens. Predicate (phase==1)&(L>=8) has recall 0.97 / mass recall 0.98 but precision 0.14. Adding the first-token set j/t/u/k/v gives F1 0.54 on dev (precision 0.51, mass recall 0.74); with first_tok==j alone precision is 0.86 but recall 0.19. It does not fire in the copy phase, or on L<=6 sequences. The leftover structure (graded first-token preference, plus some unexplained variation inside each first token) keeps a crisp boolean from reaching high F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: j, t, u, k, v, s; least: 1, q, l, x) and the previous input (most: h, i, m, x, d, r; least: 2, t, q, w); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=9, L=9 & t=8.
